label: rem:julia-hausdorff-dimension-prediction
title: Hausdorff-dimension prediction $d_H(q)$ of the Reeb Julia set
html:
The S_{\mathrm{cell}} closure fixing G_{\mathrm{Planck}} = 1 (gravitational constant) yields a prediction for the Hausdorff dimension of the Reeb Julia set. This provides an independently checkable claim against transfer-operator computations.

Hausdorff dimension prediction. The corrected formula predicts:

  d_H(q) =  \frac{(2q-1)^2}{q^3}.
q d_H predicted d_H box-counting Known exact Note
1 1.000 — 1.000 (unit circle) Exact match
q_0 1.088 1.012 — Box-counting underestimates thin quasicircles
1.5 1.185 — — Basilica root c = -3/4 (period-2 parabolic; known d_H \sim 1.2)
\varphi^2 1.000 — — Golden crossover: d_H returns to 1

The formula yields d_H = 1 at q = 1 (unit circle) and q = (3+\sqrt{5})/2 = \varphi^2 (golden threshold), which are exact matches. For 1 < q < \varphi^2, the Julia set is strictly more fractal than a circle (d_H > 1), consistent with McMullen's theorem [mcmullen1998].

Testable prediction. The value d_H(q_0) = 1.088 is testable against high-precision transfer-operator computations (Ruelle 1982) for d_H(J_c) at c(0.1097) = 0.338 + 0.073i. Box-counting gives d_H \approx 1.012 but systematically underestimates thin Jordan curves. The Ruelle perturbative lower bound 1 + |c|^2/(4\ln 2) \approx 1.043 is consistent with our prediction.
